# The map of material science

From what we have listed after which the Cold War happened, it is easy to get yourself lost in the land of which material science bases itself in. Indeed of such, the phase right now of history can be considered of the proliferation of the old day material science, much to the disdain of the practitioners standing inside it. Before studying in details of what to entail of the development thereof, we might as well consider the map of material science, from the relative ancient age to the present, and settle a few definitions, operationally speaking that will evolute within times. 

## Pre-material science

The history has not been so kind to the precursors of material science on itself. During much course of histories, material science has been staying in the lane of *intriguing but disfranchising* field of accumulated research, specifically targeting certain parts of the material landscape. The definition of *material*, even up to present, is largely incoherent thereof, that it would be difficult to classify of what to be material, as some may even argue that water is a type of material, or it can be a solvent, or it can be a neutral medium. But it just so happens that the current landscape of material science, as of in the past, remains the same. The concept of material has never been given a rigorous, stable and agreed definition across the traditions that constitute materials science. The definition has changed rapidly, repeatedly, each change reflecting a different commitment, not realization, not unification or reverse calibration, but rather to about what kinds of things exist and what kinds of relations between things are scientifically fundamental, if such is even possible thereof. 

History of pre-material science can be separated into the concept word of **matter**. Before the Greek philosophical tradition formalized the concept of matter, there was already a practical concept of material that craftsmen used, shaped and transformed. Those are of the precursor materials, specifically, *bronze, iron, clay wood, flax, ivory, stone*, and so on. How do they feel of those? Specifically through *crude inference*, where one makes it so that their property is reflected by a certain metric of utilization or interaction. For example, one can say between bronze and iron, there exists a specific kind of *hardness* in contact with others, the hardness of manipulation, extraction, and sleight of handling. Cyril Stanley Smith, noted in 1968 that material is the matter of which have been through a relation toward human practice and use, most often so. This practical, relational conception of material was the implicit framework of artisans, craftsmen, and metallurgists from antiquity through the early modern period, much to the disdain of those requiring a more fundamental concept. But even so, it makes sense - matter exists as the wider universal encompassing dilemma of which everything would follow in. Even human exists of matter. Aether, luminiferous aether of the mechanical aether of sort, in which light was supposed to travel in-between, also uses the concept of matter. The Maxwell field equations specifically targetting $(\mathbf{E},\mathbf{B})$ conjunctive fields are also a form of 'matter', if we are to speak of the same criteria [^1]. The problem and difficulty there of, lies in the consequence - it means that the same substance can be simultaneously a material in one context and matter in another - it depends on the anthropological baseline of whatever using it. Such is rather very centric toward the craftsmen, but we soon realized that the world is not only us. The difficulty and the quest to find such, begins with this relational, context-dependent concept and forcing it to the becoming of being universal, of which we might as well say to be independent. We constitute the first act:

[^1]: It is of certain observation that only the concept of *material aether* was rejected. At all, the notion of aether was never refuted, but transubstantiated into a newer form.

> **Act I.** (Baseline of utilization)
>
> Material can be defined, in difference to matter, by of which it makes sense for usage of certain actor at will. That is, if such matter is of meaning to manipulate and utilization for a certain person, then it becomes material. 

Up to another region of time, or so we speak of, Thales of Miletus regarded water as sole fundamental building block of matter, and thus henceforth also material itself.  He held that water, in taking different forms, constitutes the earth, atmosphere, sky, mountains, gods and men, beasts and birds, grass and trees, and animals down to worms, flies and ants. All these are different forms of water, and for certainty many of such different qualities inside many matter or materials, would be derivation simply by manipulating water, of which is the ability we do not possess of the time (yet). 

![I cannot find a picture about the **water theory** in historical records of illustration, so make due with sewerage and drainage systems: (a) Minoan (photo: A.N. Angelakis) and (b) Indus Valley figure, then. Taken from [@w14193149].](img/plumbing_thales.png)

This constitutes the second action, the **action of fumdamentalizing derivation**. Basically speaking, this requires the think that there exists, out of all set $\{\mathrm{Ma},\mathrm{Me}\}$ for material and matter of arbitrary choice on classification notion (where we can still take the anthropological definition for material), to have certain *initial form* that would make up literally everything else in existence, just with more details or more complex types. That is, the *minimal framework* itself. It is understandable how Thales would have thought of such - consider water, a *fluid* as we know of now, where shape can be transformed, the basis of life and what human (anthropological basis, mind you) cannot live without, the solvent of many processes, medium for many mechanical or proto-chemical purposes. All of such constitutes to the big picture of that water is fundamental, and we cannot really fail that to a given degree of sort. 

> **Act II.** (Fundamentalization of derivatives on initials)
>
> Material can be considered a set of **matter**, or rather, the set of all manipulable and utilized matter of interest, where its origin is fixated to become from an initial point or an initial starting substrate, for which derivations of such substrates are used to explain the classification thereof. 

The problem with Thales's choice - water - however, is immediately visible. If water is the fundamental substance of all things, then the water being drunk, the water that is flowing in a river, the water sitting in a bowl, the water flowing in rivers, all of which would be equally *material* in the most basic sense, it serves the purpose of being the functionally invariant structure. But what about iron or any form of *metals*? Iron cannot be water in any obvious sense. True, that up to now molecular structures can be recombined, and perhaps we can use them to make iron, but that is still excruciatingly hard, and most of the time not even worth the time to do such. Thales must have held that iron is somehow a transformation of water, water to be in a very different form. This means transforming the definition of water to be distant from its normal usage, to something of which is not water but the description of *fluid*, that is, 

> The underlying substrate that can take many forms, one which looks like what we call water. 

But this then fails when you encounter oil, or anything of such form. At that point, you have proliferation of origin - what to be called as the initials, oil or water? A sidestep can also happen if we get the Second Thales of Miletus - regarding a substance $X$ to be the unified form of which iron can be made of its derivation. But it just so happens that there are also many forms of things that look like iron, but does not act like iron in any form. This again, means pluralism of definition and the redefinition stack of which will dilute the meaning of the origin to be said of. 

Coincidentally or not based on our projection, this is the first appearance of a pattern that will recur throughout the entire history - the concept chosen as fundamental for "material" turns out to require extensive redefinition in order to accommodate everything it needs to accommodate, until the word means something quite different from its ordinary usage, while the ordinary usage remains operational in practice alongside the philosophical redefinition. Beside from confusion, it also incurs the cost - of which to ask *exactly where are you going* toward, of those redefinitions until oblivion? Such is rather hard to answer, in which because partly of the form to base anything to be fundamental, incurs also the uncertainty that there might be the *more fundamental point* that disarm what we have been doing, right above. In fact, Anaximenes substituted air for water; Heraclitus, fire. Empedocles proposed all four — earth, water, air, and fire — as irreducible elements. Aristotle based his argument chiefly on the analysis of "becoming" or substantial change. Those are also pluralism, but now in the concept of *elements* - different categorization of substrates, of which is rather antique but intuitive, and thus giving such the baseline for which all would follow. The argument of Aristotle is also interesting. He based his argument chiefly on, paraphrased,

> If $A$ is converted to $B$ of a process $T(\cdot)$, then there **must exist** something of common between them, without such no conversion can be done. 

This is presupposing the atomic theory, in which we know that atoms, and many small sub-partitions thereof are responsible for such allowance of transitions as the 'reference point fundamental substrate', so to speak. But so far, those elements are still categorization of which cannot be measurable of manipulable properties. How do you quantify 'wetness' of water? Similarly to fire, how do you quantify the 'fireness' of certain elements, if they are to be derived from such? Can iron be only earthen being with certain amounts of some elemental form elsewhere? Not quite so, and indeed not so trivial. Even if in the set of no transformation, but merely successions by the annihilation of the first term - $A$ subjects - and the creation of the second - $B$ objects - it is still probable of such fact to say it relies less on the property baseline indicted upon. Those are *external labels* that we made ourselves, much to the disdain of people of the time, simply is not enough, even if it is thermodynamically interesting, anticipating something like a property-space description of phases. But in all, they are not sufficient, and one can find the breaking point anywhere one shall like to do so, and no one would be able to answer within the box of which those are to be accepted of. However, his point about conversion is right up to a certain point. Two objects in existence that are *transformed* from one to another, posits the fact that they are somewhat connected enough that you can morph one to another, so it means, basically that $A$ and $B$ must have something in common, no matter how small it is or weak it can be. This applies to also matter - you cannot transform water to iron because at the fundamental ordinary frame, they have nothing in common aside from being 'of existence and interaction'. But, there will *always* be the common point - the word existence themselves. What lies after we crumble all of those objects? In one way or another, against such question, most philosophers and those of thoughts at such time, turned to *hylomorphism* as their saving grace. 

### In-detail - the Aristotle's Hylomorphism

Per the subject topic, of which more philosophical than not, in @Ainsworth2016FormMatter it was to be said that Aristotle's hylomorphism is rather advanced for its time. The philosophical doctrine of such posits that all physical entities are compounds of **matter** (*hyle* - the material constituent or potentiality) and **form** (*morphe or eidos - the structure essence or actuality*), to explain of the material and the world. 

![The Hylomorphism in Aristotle's Theory](img/hylomorphism.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

The notion is toward what are essentially **compositional thought**, for Aristotle of his general ideas. Aristotle defines matter as to be 'out of which' something is made. For example, letters are the matter of syllables. Thus, matter is a relative term: an object counts as matter relative to something else. Clay is matter relative to a brick because a brick is made of clay, at that specific point, whereas bricks are matter relative to a brick house. Change is analyzed as a material transformation, for where matter is what undergoes a change of form. In all, it is also the *relational composition* that marks the strength of this approach, and perhaps even now this line of thought has only been refined, much not disappeared entirely, because of the act it allows that would be central to pretty much the *way down toward atomic scale*, and so on.

> **Act III**: We presuppose matter to be *relative*, such that $A$ is mater to $B$, if $B$ is made of $A$. Thus, matter notion are *compositional*, and at such *relational* to a given degree. 

Such relational definition of matter is rather philosophically sophisticated, if one is to claim such, which is fair for what it is worth of. For Aristotle, "matter" is not a name for some particular stuff as opposed to Thales's thesis - but rather of the *relation* between objects of being. $X$ is the matter of $Y$ when $Y$ is made from $X$. This means the same stuff can be simultaneously matter, of a statue, and something that itself has matter, relative to copper and tin. There is no ultimate substratum - or if there is, of which rather an effort of such to be *prime matter*, it is also indeterminate as to be philosophically contentious (no one wants to seriously debate that again, for all it's worth of). 

The hierarchical, level-relative concept of material bears a striking, but not so surprising resemblance of structures to the multiscale architecture of modern materials science. At each level of the hierarchy, there is something that functions as matter to be the *lower level*. Then, there exists something that functions as the form binding in which makes those lower levels higher. It does not say much about what constitute the higher layer - there can be many and of extremely complex form for all the practitioner would care for, and it would still be there of the indeterminacy of such. Each level has its own characteristic form, and the explanation of properties at each level invokes the form at that level, not the form at lower levels. 

Speaking of such, then why this is not utilized now? It seems that the theory can be adapted, much more general than it can be of any, which is a nice thing to have. Changing the context, and such would be complete as for a new modern explanation? Unfortunately, Aristotle's commentators and thereof of himself, have been struggling with a quite non-trivial set of tensions, all of which testimony has been made that the structure is unstable on itself. For this, even if we ignore one of the fundamental problem of such that can be avoided by directly supervising the structure on the precision of mathematics - which would organize his anticipation of the structural-property relationship, there are still many forms in which the problem pervades of what to be presented of. 

1. Firstly, Aristotle thinks of such as that,  if one pursues this hierarchy of matter far enough downwards, Aristotle believes that one will reach the four elements. The *presupposition* of the four elements is simply false and conditioned of the knowledge of the time. Even if right now we presuppose one for convenience, what can we even do? There exists no determinated origin point of which we can say where will we reach. Such is to abandon the *prime matter* itself, but that begs the question of how far can we go down? 
2. The theory still retains its **ontological paralysis**. Even if now we have been saying of the relational structure to be quite as good as it can be, the structure is paralyzed under its own statement. Suppose that $X$ is made of $A,B,C$. Similarly, $Y$ is made of $A,B,D$. Both $X,Y$ are variations of the same copper linage, or steel, which itself is currently known as a compound. By such, the lower level of $\{A,B,C,D\}$ contains two set of matters overlapped to give two current-layer subjects. However, they are the same under certain categorization scheme. How should we quantify this? How much of $D$ can be settled of its form in this setting, for example? When they function in the same way, used the same way, approximately having the same setting and relational utilization to the being in usage - the anthropological baseline - what to be separated from them? Similarly, if two objects are inherently different, even though they use the exactly same set, full set of matters of which are lower-level of such, how do you compare them and distinguish them? This requires adding more information, but that might also expand if you proliferate into more complex settings, more difficult distinguishment and characterization regime, until you have quite a mess. What can we do under such? 
3. Another tension, which have been there for a long time now, is the naturalness of the relationship between form and matter. Is the form just accidentally related to the matter, or it is essentially related to it? Can we remove it or replace it and the 'matter' afterward still be legitimate? The system and its frame are simply too big and too generalized, that it fails even its own test. The same structure even appears in modern materials science. The question of whether form is essential or accidental to matter is precisely the question of whether a material is defined by its composition or by its processing history. Carbon can be graphite or diamond, same matter different form, where the form is not merely accidental, but neither is the form essential to the carbon in the sense that carbon must take one form rather than another. Carbon materials can be just carbon materials, with its orientation changed, and nothing would break. Aside from the diamond. 

To pull this out apart, we might as well turn our attention to the **Scientific Revolution**, and the subsequent **Industrial-Chemical Revolutions** for their insights. But let us summarize what have been observed of the all three failures, and possibly more if one wants to look enough to the picture. 

#### Peaking - The Medieval Elaboration

Of the long-time of the Medieval period, scholasticism inherited of Aristotle through Arabic translation, primary through Avicenna and Averroes, elaborated hylomorphism into an intricate theological and metaphysical system. Those using the concept frequently distinguished between substantial form and accidental form, if one can even distinguish such from the description that is poorly operated of. For Thomas Aquinas, he argued that everything in the natural world is created by God and has specific purpose, which is revealed though both divine revelation, or natural philosophy. Such is rather characteristic of the Christian thought centred around which there are god to be, but also to set a baseline that would be rather biased, as far as we know of the present - it presupposes the purpose as already defined, of what claimed to be relational. Which is, in certain form, contradiction of sort. 

Nothing much can be said about this part more than this, unfortunately. The distinguishment scheme is rather deliberate but flawed, for example, 

> A substantial form is what makes a thing the kind of thing it is — for a piece of bronze, its substantial form is what makes it bronze rather than tin or lead. An accidental form is a property that the thing has but could lose while remaining the same kind of thing — the shape of a bronze statue is accidental, because the bronze can be melted and recast without ceasing to be bronze. 

Even if such to be extended far beyond of all creations, said statement is simply unwarranted of its determination. Tin, lead, bronze, are those that would be subjected to label, of different characteristics and structural properties in determining such. However, the determination is not discrete, there can be bronze-with-a-bit-of-tin, or bronze but designed to be at certain point, still the same substrate, but now similar to copper. And so on. Accidental form is easily to see, the shape is *accidental*, but also making contradiction - it can be melted, it can be into liquid form, but then would the extracted form being accidental? Why bronze just not appear in life as to be the melted form or a big blob? By then, what is even accidental anymore? 

### In-detail - the Mechanical and Chemical Revolution

Of the mechanical and chemical revolution, due of the 18th century to the down of the 19th century, a series of landmarks *patents* and *researches* were made, given the way possible of what there is to be the material science in the new dawn age. The two landmarks of the biggest kind can be served as present. 

- The 17th Century foundation of the **mechanical philosophy** of Descartes, Gassendi, Boyle, and Newton performed a philosophical operation on the concept of material, that has shaped material ever since. We cannot truly comprehend of what the consequences are, but it would like to be thought of still being worked out, even by modern mechanisms. There are many concepts evolved of the time, for Boyle to be *individual bit* or *formational characteristics*, of size, shape, orientation, order and textures, being matter completely passive and inert. For Descartes, the notion of *duality* took place, for where there exists again the *inertness* of the subject matter, then comes the exclusion of all *psychic characteristic* of which earlier of history being framed to be material nature, and forces physical nature to be inert and devoid of sources of activity on its own - such distinction is rather very strong, and legacy of such thought remains in the entire body of physics still of present.

In such, would rather to be said, the theory that we know right now of the **Newtonian mechanics**, bears the most responsibility of the transition. Newtonian physics, in general, inherited and fleshed out positions of Boyle, and Descartes, of which to be the physical reality being acted upon, for those mechanical philosophies stated imply the advocation of **corpuscular structures**, and *microstructure constitution*. In retrospect, individual 'small parts' arrange themselves into corpuscular structure that gives a substance its various properties. Different corpuscular structure account for different substances and different properties. As far as we consider, Boyle's corpuscular theory is, an second early version, after Aristotle's, of the **structure-property relationship**, where the microstructure of the corpuscles determines the properties of the bulk material. While mechanical in nature, as it relies on size, shape, arrangement, motions - replacing form by geometry - essentially [^2], it is still a granted substantial contribution, for the elimination of any teleological or dispositional explanation from material science. Matter now does not have indicted meaning of the higher-order being, nor the existence thereof for such matter to be *aware*, as for it to gain purposes. But rather, it makes due of what there is, for which components it shares of existence in the form of becoming. 

[^2]: It is good to stop and note that, even of the current form, the philosophical question of what to be the **form** of the object is still under heavy debate. Though, as it currently stands, it would be a nice change of pace to stop and transfer it to another framework itself, rather than sticking to such term. 

Newtonian physics patched up the operational ideal of such form separation by co-author of sort the position similar to what Boyle and Descartes have done (post-instantiation, in one way of speaking), by removing the object from its force inside his developed analytical framework. A force is *exerted*, and of its foundation if none of such force are at present, the state of the object simple stays the same, so to speak. The object becomes *potential*, of properties, of mass, of momentum, whatever, of what to be the properties and dynamics that follows. One subtle consequence of such, is thus before any interaction can be made, they are effectively of the expression, to be decoupled from each other and bear no relevance from either side. It foreshadows an aspect - to truly see properties of object, there exists the requirement of *interaction per specification*. This means, in simple term, that by decoupling the two, you are now asking the question: *how do you see it?* Of course, you cannot objectively see it, as per definition of 'giving out' properties require you to touch it, ordinarily speaking, or *probe it under experiments*, strictly speaking. But this on itself is an act of interaction and **methodological intervention**. Such is, there is no view of the pure potential aside from those you presuppose to be minimal, such is also how most of the time we approximate subjects - negligible, supposing air frictions as such, supposing interaction does not move the objects, so on so forth. There exists, as such scheme on itself, any way to get properties of an object further than the identification that *such object exists*, which implicitly requires subtle interaction - either by its deformation and illumination of a luminiferous object toward us that we can see of its existence, or by various interaction of which finally we obtain of the relevant resultant of such. In a sense, surprisingly speaking, existence-identification is already a form of measurement, which at best of the viewport, there is no pre-observational baseline at all. You would either have to get the snapshot of time, and presuppose linearity or uniformity of behaviours, and predict the *previous state*, while simultaneously the *future states*, where states here is defined operationally simple as the snapshot in which the *being*, under certain description, contains certain amount of information that describe it of which quantity or of what properties. Conjuring such, the thesis is breached - there is no view from nowhere onto the object's properties. Every observation is already an intervention, the mechanical philosophy's dream of reading off fixed corpuscular properties hits the wall of its own dynamics, by its own language, of its own virtue. 

Simplification, as we called of such, also appears in the corpuscular itself. There exists the fundamental problem at that stage with the notion of *continuity* and *discreteness*, of such is born out of the philosophy in which we are to say, each form of object presupposes the layer below it to provide 'small components' that would form the bricks and mortars of the house. However, such is rather unclear how to dissect of it, rather than to presuppose that there exists the absolute form at the lower end of the spectrum, to be the *prime matter*, as of such returned to Aristotle baseline. But every baseline can be reduced to such as to ask, would there be any lower-level substrates that *support* also the prime matter? How would that be verified of said descriptions? In a sense, *point mass* is a notion used in Newtonian physics to hand-wave such notion - by making concentration to a singular, dimensionless point, forgoing any volumetric uncertainty where one now introduces the volume approximation, and both the volume of the corpuscle itself. But that does not indict that reality has to be this way, but rather again another simplification of approximation of reality. We can see this, actually, when we move onto rigid-object dynamics, where one again uses those *point masses constructions* for the rigid object. However, density of such can only be gauged, up to a certain point, and the point-mass object under such description is *enumerative-wise large*, $N\to \infty$ if able as to fully fill in all the admissible space created by the model. By then, a simplification scheme is again made, returning to the *volumetric sub-volume*, on and on and on, until that we redefine point mass as to be the relative *minimal volumetric space*. But doing so inadvertently contradicts both the baseline, and the certainty of partition. The corpuscular itself is then not corpuscular, and its form is conditioned on the volumetric space of the larger system, where now the rigid object stays in such form because of other 'corpuscle'. Which is a rather roundabout problem of the structure itself [^3], and ironically, which is precisely what the mechanical philosophy was trying to escape from in Aristotle - relational, context-dependent identity. Another dilemma is also to break the prime matter entirely, because now, once you allow the point mass to become a minimal sub-volume, you immediately face the question of how to partition the volume. Different partitioning schemes give different "corpuscles" for the same object. Which partition is the real one? The framework has no answer because the partition is chosen by the modeller and of which designers are there for computational convenience, not discovered in the object. The corpuscles are as much considered of being artifacts of the description as features of reality it presupposes.

- The **Mechanical Revolution**, or *First Industrial Revolution*, of which mechanized textile production, mining, iron-making, transport, and many, is one such factor where the role of material science drifted. Certainly, of [@mohajan2019firstIR],[@sharma2022_materials_timeline],[@mitrovic2022_watt],[@watt1769_patent],[@klein2007_materials],[@taylor2007_review_klein], they depended on new materials and on evolving ways of thinking about materials, in the same time such philosophical intervention are made. Coke-smelted iron (Abraham Darby's patent) provided cast iron in abundance never seen before; Darby's Coalbrookdale works cast over 100 Newcomen steam-engine cylinders by 1758, showing iron production scaling with steam technology. By 1779 Darby’s descendants built one of the first cast-iron bridges (Ironbridge) and in 1802 the first steam locomotive, illustrating that new metalworking methods enabled entirely new structures. As materials became central, scientific study of them expanded: 18th-century metallurgists (e.g. Réaumur, Grignon) began examining crystal structures in iron and alloy behaviour (see [@taylor2007_review_klein]). Historians by then, note that chemists and engineers started treating substances as defined “objects of inquiry” with measurable properties. The question came out from the mechanical era is rather distinct, as to almost abandon the ontology into the question to the *classification problem* and identification itself, to metallurgy, to characterization, and many of such are detrimental as the workhorse of the revolution itself. Out of every patent and revolution landmarks stated, only one single work of James Watt to be the introduction of the core thermodynamic concepts. Even then, the concept itself is highly operational - it presupposes the function and bears no mind to the separation of matter and properties. Here, they are both the embodiment of the same object - the *subject 'matter'*, having both properties, and of its matter functional states. Now, objects would be characterized by their shape and forms, mass, interactions, behaviours, boiling points, operational quantities in operation of interaction. We are to then admit that as is, the separation simply does not make any sense operationally, because an object at rest, similar to what Smith used to characterize of the old philosophy - relational to the worker and industrial machinery. How that is reconciled to the crux of Newtonian mechanics, which secretly or not presupposed the latter is itself an interesting question, but not the main one at this point. The question now turns to the final pillar of which to explain, even if operationally, what can the compositions to the macroscopic down to the microscopic be of? The answer, of course, at this point, would be atoms of the time, but that requires a separated revolution on its own. 

The question here is valid. At this stage of the scientific body, the matter-properties distinction is operationally meaningless. What is of use to think about an object for its matter, and for its properties to be different, while working with them, they seem to be one? Object is also only accessible via interaction, as far as we see of what we established. Corpuscles again introduced the uncertainty and arbitrary partition dependency again, *after works*. The identity itself is replaced of Aristotle precondition of **relationalism** - you cannot sufficiently determine the ground at where and of what, without the circular circus being relevant to the picture. The question now that 

> What kind of theory could restore determinacy without reintroducing naive ontology? Can such theory restore or at least attempt to, of object identity and classification after the collapse of intrinsic properties, without reintroducing arbitrary metaphysical primitives, or not?

The solution, of the mechanical elaboration, ironically, operationally collapsed the matter/properties separation that the mechanical philosophy had just spent a century carefully constructing. Granted, we do not actually know of it if the matter-properties ontology is physically relevant and provides us with a schematic of such for understanding closer to what we presuppose as the true object itself. But collapsing such for the purpose of operational success is rather hiding the debt away, until we finally reach the ladder rung where those questions are again valid. The only problem within such way, is that while the revolution that the mechanical philosophy made possible - industrialization - produced a material practice that implicitly contradicted the mechanical philosophy's own ontology, it is worse that such action remain *hidden* inside its own framework, just as we have mentioned earlier during the Newtonian cascade, of the separation itself, the theory being successful but hiding the uncomfortable question about *relativeness* and *inference*, of which later would be the absolute boundary that the frame fails, thus implicitly leads to the new theory about the restricted *frame* on itself. And so, where the frame of the mechanical nature is failing secretly, what is holding it together is the demand for the atomic theory, which is to supplant of *the chemical revolution*. In all, the purpose of the Chemical Revolution is the **forced hand of precision**, where theory comes to demand more and more grounding of what to be *invariant*, unchanged, of identity. And, it is to note trivial of present, it is not the first attempt (or maybe it is), and also not the final answer. 

-  Due of Antoine Lavoisier's chemical revolution, of which is the central part to overturn **phlogiston theory**, sparked the newer term of which now we saw as the *modern chemical science* era. The analysis is rather delicate, and should be taken into consideration. Due of history, before Lavoisier made his progresses, Georg Ernst Stahl as the German chemist of the old day, proposed what we now call as *phlogiston*, of which being the intangible substance released from fermentation, combustion and relevant processes of the kind (note that this is deliberately *arbitrary*). Thus, every object or matter in consideration of a specific interaction process, forgoing the question of matter-property but to treat it as plain *object* of distinguishment, to be of specific amount of $\mathrm{Ph}(A)$ for object class $A$. During combustion, then for example, phlogiston was thought to be expelled into air, resulting in a *dephlogisticated* residue, such as wood ash (see more in [here](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/history/stahls-phlogiston-theory)). On the surface, it seems probable, as during such transformation process, there exists the *residue* of which we can see of the transformation being $A\to B+ C$, where $C$ is the ash and $B$ is the product (we are doing process schema here). The question of *how $C$ were there*, in the first place, is the Aristotle question asked of the lower level, and here Stahl predicated it with phlogiston. How Lavoisier disproved it? Well, not by operating within the framework itself, because the framework is sound in its question of deliverance - there must be something that give rise to such combustion residue - the residue does not really look like $A$, nor it is similar to what $B$ produced. So there are external factors, or, in this case, another *internal factor* of itself in the subject that would only be released by interaction in the kind of combustion (here, is the interaction picture). Instead, Lavoisier attempted the experiment to show that combustion involves oxygen that transform the subject itself. This targets a rather simple case - metal rust, where the object actually during the process increases of volume instead of reducing, of which supposedly reducing in phlogiston during the process set up a kind of *internal conservation law* within itself - that phlogiston + matter would stay the same instead; which, evidently, is not the case. As of such, we have the following empirical refutation of which one made to disprove at such boundary. 

> Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier, the most prominent antiphlogistonist, believed that calcination produced a weight gain in metals because something in the air combined with the metal. He repeated the experiments of Priestley, interpreting the change in the lead calx as the loss of a gas into the air. This explanation solved the problem of weight gain experienced by metals when calcinated: Lavoisier reasoned that the same gas that a calcinated metal released had bonded to it when it was originally calcinated, and the weight of the gas had been added to the weight of the pure metal at that time. Lavoisier named this new gas “oxygen.” Although Lavoisier was never able to dissuade Priestley from believing in phlogiston, he did convince most other chemists of his day that the theory needed to be discarded. [^4]

[^4]: Even then, we can see that not even Lavoisier can convince the phlogistonists such as Priestley himself. His experiment is rather sound, however despite popular beliefs and what to be considered of the narrative refutation. In one, he heated some calx of lead (mercuric oxide) in a closed container and found that the air released by the calx caused a candle to burn more vigorously and that a mouse placed in the container could breathe longer than when placed in normal air. Priestley called the air inside the container “dephlogisticated air”: He assumed that, by heating lead calx, he had removed phlogiston from normal air and caused it to be reabsorbed by the calx. In fact, rather than removing something from the air, Priestley had added to it when the heated mercuric oxide gave off **oxygen**. Without the knowledge nor the realization of the breaking case, one would have to see that the evidences inside, suggested phlogiston to be rather right. 

The ontological baseline now shifted, where phlogiston is actually the *substance air* of which combine to give the effect a stable cause. The question again shifted toward, what is even air? How would air combines with the matter of metal to produce combustion? The layer is now clarified quite a bit, as for there must be *something smaller* that make up both the metal, and both the air, for them to interact and give rise to residue, albeit of the same mass for both as it is. It is also a rather early entry to the concept of entropy and energy transformation - if we are to have same mass, accumulated throughout air giving in to give rise to rust and so on, then during the process of burning, we lose the torch and of the fire soon fade. Then, what is transformed, and what was lost during that process? Such question would be answered later, or rather not, as the body of science already gave its way toward it, and we should not reinvent nor reinterpreting it, lest of the space available in the discourse such is this small section. That said, we now have the *conservation law of Mass*, where now mass of constituent, actually can be traced to specific interaction partners of the process, not merely attribute more to what there exists. Such is also again, a problem of which still surfaces as of the modern context - *how do you characterize materials good enough to get that distinction*, and should that be answered, many would be elucidated of the process. For now, the revolution points itself to the quality of which that can be *qualified*, for the first time in many decades of works. 

Let us end the section by taking on the implications thereof for this linage of itself, and of the chemical revolution in its entirety. Namely, the technological 'marvel' thereof. For what to be seen from [@acs_lavoisier_landmark], [@acs_priestley_landmark], [@flavell-while2011_leblanc], [@roebuck_lead_chamber_1746], [@britannica_arkwright], [@britannica_hargreaves], [@britannica_cartwright], and of [@britannica_wilkinson] for what history preserved of intentions and records, the Chemical Revolution indeed made the depth of how materials were to be defined, albeit with the same constraints we set above. 

> Klein & Lefèvre show that 18th-century chemists developed a new ontology of substances: they identified and categorized “pure chemical substances” by composition. For example, air was re-ontologized into oxygen, nitrogen, etc. Traditional "affinity tables" of the pre-1789 era (organizing *substances* by *reaction affinities*) gave way to Lavoisier’s Tableau de nomenclature chimique (1787), classifying substances by **elemental makeup**[^5]. 

[^5]: Again, we note the lower-level commitment here as non-trivial. It will recur in later organization. 

Much can be said of the later work, i.e. Dalton's **atomic theory** to enhance such, and also to explain of what to be said from our analysis, to be of the following incursion. The atomic theory helped in the way of the forced hand of description, during which it proposed:

1. All **matter** is composed of extremely small indivisible particles called *atoms*. 
2. Atoms, of a given element are identical in size, mass and other properties. Atoms of different elements differ in size, mass and other properties. Such is to say, we have the *atomic species*, or, *elements*. 
3. Atoms cannot be subdivided, created or destroyed. That is, atoms of an element are not changed into atoms of a different element during chemical reaction. 
4. Atoms of different elements combined in simple whole number ratios to form chemical compounds. 
5. In chemical reactions, atoms are combined, separated or rearranged. 
6. In a given compound, the relative number and kind of atoms are constant. 

Supported by again, Lavoisier, alongside the set of *empirical law* on **conservation of mass**, the law of **definite proportions**, and **law of constant composition**, and, lastly, **multiple proportions**. What is said, however, is that the apparent contradiction of the grounding to shut down the lower-level constituent, has been settled. What to be lower than the atom itself is not in the question but delegated into impossibility - we simply cannot reach. In a sense, and of the period, such worked spectacularly within the domain where such grounding is applicable. History, however, writes itself. And so far, before we move on to diagnose the failure of such, we are set one account that by virtue of our currently knowledge only, would be contingent to the realization. The *quark* was being idle. 

For industrial chemistry itself, the new chemistry indeed gained operational success, especially of large-scale chemical manufacturing process. The two often cited prospect arose to be as followed, 

- **Sulphuric acid**: John Roebuck’s *lead-chamber process* (1746) allowed bulk acid production. By lining wooden reaction chambers with lead, Roebuck’s method produced concentrated sulphuric acid at far lower cost. This massive supply of acid fuelled textiles, metallurgy and later fertilizers.
- **Soda ash**: Nicolas Leblanc devised a process (patented 1791) to make soda from common salt and sulphuric acid. Leblanc’s method "turned soda production from *nothingness* to a major industry". His 1791 patent was lauded as "very superior" in economy and purity. Mid-19th century production reached ~400,000 tons/year. These early chemical plants (sulphuric acid, soda) were among the first examples of the modern chemical industry.

At last, from 1780s, the shift has been to be foundational - where substances were identified, individuated, ordered per specification of certain dialect, and classed on the basis of their composition. ## Modern scientific theories on material sciences

It is rather undermining to start the section about what to be said of *material science* to be an elaboration from what industrial and chemical revolution are to be of. And, under just the behest of what to come, I commit to that position. I simply posit the simple directive that under the very process of the 19th-20th-21st century of now, what we have been seeing and patching, is the patchwork of many, if not proliferation of pluralism in itself, to what as to be said of the same ground, with cartography stretched from not Europe but to the American Continent - just that we ought to mistake it for India.

About at the end of the Lavoisier-Dalton revolution onward, the artefact remains the two criteria of material sciences. What to be said to be incompatible, and of which to be said of not the same. 

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}

### Criterion CR.1. 

A material/matter is identified by its composition - its elemental makeup and molecular structure. Two samples with the same composition are the same material, since their constituent parts are the same. 

:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}

### Criterion CR.2. 

A material/matter is identified by its functional behaviour in context - its response to processing, performance in utilization and application, and its participation to be configured in activation relation. Two samples with the same composition with different processing histories are different materials, **if they perform differently**. 

:::

This inherent contradiction lives within the mechanical revolution and chemical revolution practical consideration, and the principle of such to be said of the atomic constituent model itself. On one side, there is the insistence on **Aristotle invariance**, where the lower level is fundamental enough as to dissolve the *dynamics*, of which for when the matter itself is utilized [^6], it would be the same material in all and of all. One the other side, there exists the **functional invariance** of the observable set - which is to say in plain language of the worker man as to be *if it works, it works* and *if it is the same, expect us to bang for bucks the same way*. Those two cannot live entirely of one another, without trespassing on themselves. These criteria conflict even in the simple case of graphite and diamond, and of which the cooled steel in rapid process or slow-cooling behaves different from one another of itself. If we are to believe that chemical revolution brings the grounding of two separated materials to be entirely same, yet *somewhere* they are different, one must ask: what are the properties we of which are missing of? And more importantly, if *atoms* cannot explain it of the atomic periodic table to be in the same position, will Aristotle return? The answer is yes.

### The failure of Dalton's

What to be said as the failure of Dalton's atomic theory (1808), is rather easy to unpack where it went wrong and what to be said of itself. Garnett (1996) and Bucat (1984) specified in a rather different details of the following information that we would be able to take apart from, which will be of relevant in later sections still. 

7. Gas particles are evenly scattered in an enclosed space and there are empty space between particles.
8. Particles move slower in liquids and vibrate about fixed positions in solids.
9. Particles join together in simple consistent ratios when two different substances react to form a third substance.
10. Mass is conserved in these reactions.
11. The spacing between solid-solid, liquid-liquid and gas-gas particles is close to 1:1:10 (Andersson, 1990; de Vos and Verdonk, 1996).

Many years apart, the story often presented in the corpus of chemical science would be of the atomic theory since Dalton, and the current **molecular kinetic theory**, though much more antique in consideration against quantum chemistry, are actually closer than what we thought. The current molecular story only imported the higher resolution of the consequence of Dalton's - such is where atoms would be still, the driving force, and their behaviours are explainable in the sense of which their connections, topology, reactions are derivable with precision of the rulesets to follow along, and it should always be that way. Or not, as we would find out. But for now, let us take apart each of them, one by one.

Then, we posit that certain element of $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ are equal only if the **properties** attached to them are of the same quantitative evaluation, we call  this $\{p\}$. Chemical reaction happens when sufficient condition are there to mix between $N_{1}+N_{2}$. Now, the key point of Dalton is that

of all whole number, for $k_{1}$ the units of element of $N_{1}$, and so on for $k_{2}$. ### Cracking the barriers

The 89 years of which will follow to Dalton from Thomson (the pudding) is very structurally interesting, and it underlies the current landscape itself of what there are of the tension between theoretical notions, and the practical layering that makes up the bulk of it. Analytically speaking, it is the sequence of four distinct crises, each of which put pressure on the Daltonian framework from a different question, systematically revealing that the postulates are hiding something underneath, for example, the atomic specificity of non-destruction. Each of which the framework would survive by deferral rather than resolution, which cumulatively being the weakening effect of the programme. Often, we jumped simply from Dalton to Thomson without much thought about what constitutes in between, though history would be said otherwise - the surprise is not without warning, but the resolution of a tension that had been building for nearly a century, and of which, all without impulse, led to Rutherford's. 

#### Prout's hypothesis and the atomic weight problem (1815–1860s)

Approximately seven years after Dalton, William Prout published paper sin 1815 and 1816 observing that the atomic weights of the known elements appeared to be whole multiples of the atomic weight of hydrogen, hypothesizing that the hydrogen atom was the only true fundamental object and that atoms of other element were the grouping of hydrogen atoms. The *prime matter* now returned with the flawed model of such, as we found out, but now supported by *empirical patterns* that would seem to say validate the experiment and hypothesis. But so are many prime matter theory coming before it on itself. Nevertheless, it can be regarded as the prime matter crack of the lower-level concern for the Daltonian framework. Prout is asking Act IV, internally within Dalton's own frameworks. Specifically speaking, Dalton presupposed the atomic species. However, Prout hypothesized that it is not indeed the atomic species but simply different variations of the hydrogen atoms that made up the world on and by itself, thus the model of atomic structure is instead hydrogen-base, atomically composite of hydrogen atoms instead. 

The action itself is not wrong. Indeed, when we consider the hydrogen atom, it can be said to be the simplest ever atom observed of the physical reality with its configurations. Implicitly, the Daltonian framework does not reject Prout's hypothesis, but simply just giving a *justification of compositions* for where all the atomic differentiation between different atomic species are from, in the form being the answer as *modularity*, where the simplest structure helps itself to create a newer theory. 

Let us deploy the hypothesis. Suppose that we have the set of $\mathcal{N}\equiv\{N\}$ chemical elements. Then, Daltonian framework says that they differ three fundamental categories. First, mass $m$, second, size $v$ if we are to speak of volumetric adherence, and third, $p_{1},...,p_{n}$ of certain other properties. Because of the aforementioned compound problem, we suppose the properties list would be *complexity-dependent* that would emerge inconsistently and fundamentally plural given its circumstances and setup of the empirical usages. Then, we focus on $m$ and $v$. Because $v$ as we now know, is approximately small on the order of $\mu m$, my Daltonian scale, they can be said to approximately negligible as the choice of comparison. Then, the question remains would be to distinguish one singular element from another. This pushes the question to the **atom** itself as to ask *what is the atom*? More specifically, can there be existence of the *simplest possible atom* that would explain for how it was formed? That is Prout's direction. The other direction would be the *anti-modularity formalists* in the sense of non-collapse into atom composition, but to say that in general, the atoms differ like balloon - some can be big, some can be small, but they are *configured that way* and of the same *concentration* mechanics. This foregrounds the extrapolation outside the framework, implicitly, but internally of Daltonian framework, such allows for saying of the special element $N$ from $M$, thus validates Daltonian than being extracted of the implication. Daltonian modularity search comes with a problem. How do you presuppose the singular atom? There are many choices for that. For example, $\mathrm{He}$ for helium is with currently specified atomic mass to be around $4.002602$. By the time of Daltonian precision, that equates to simply $4$. Oxygen is $15.9994$, approximately still to be $16$. Then, indeed, we can say that helium constitutes oxygen. Which is weird, because Helium cannot form Nitrogen or Boron because of the whole number requirement. Lithium (for $\mathrm{Li}$ to be $\sim 6.941$) would be close to forming Neon, as $\mathrm{Ne}\sim 20.1797$. The pattern is inconsistent, but it is rather clear from experiments, they are non-trivially large. The only candidate that would be feasible under such thinking of such, without asking the blocked move of what is even the atom, would be to take *hydrogen*, which is of approximately $1.00794$ atomic mass. The number is almost too nice, and for the precision of the time, such can be said to simple one. That is where Prout was, and how the conjecture was formed. Surprisingly however, the issue is self-referential, using its own assumptions to immunize itself against the question those assumptions generated, of which would be seen in its response against Prout. 

The Daltonian framework, by then, responded by rejecting Prout empirically. A series of more careful measurements of the atomic weights, compiled by Berzelius in 1828 and Turner in 1832, disproved quite so of the hypothesis - in particular of the atomic weight of chlorine, the proportion is $35.45$ instead, which is not whole number as said. In fact, Berzelius, the foremost analytical chemist that compiled such, said in his work to be:

> This work belongs to those few productions from which science will derive no advantage whatever [...] The greatest civility which his contemporaries can show the author, is to forget that it was ever published.

Ironically, however, the result of being $35.45$ times that of Hydrogen worked against his favour, of which would be our current atomic model of current time. Suppose that the process we have contains a chemical reaction, specifically, between chlorine, oxygen, and hydrogen. Then, it is true that oxygen and hydrogen satisfies the trivial $k/p$-ratio requirement of chemical operation. However, this means that chlorine would not. Hence, the ordering matter, which means that same compositional chemistry, different history, different impossibility result. Furthermore, if oxygen and hydrogen reaction under certain specificity produces $\mathrm{H_{2}O}$, in which dilute and *react* with chlorine to form hypochlorous acid and hydrochloric acid, then it means that the dissemination of resolution increases - the reactant must include a sub-process, and why such exists is not known. Moreover, as we know of current form, chlorine reacts vigorously with hydrogen to produce hydrogen chloride gas. This means this direct argument glossed over the inconsistency in favour of conservatism that would expand the crack in another place rather than close it - we missed an entire process, and how the process works would not be known exactly. In a sense, Berzelius invited himself to a Turkey shoot of Dalton's leg. 

In the end, Prout's question was not answered. It was suppressed by more precise atomic weight measurements that appeared to refute it, but unknowingly, also widen the cracks. Furthermore, the discovery of *isotope* in much later covered this in much specificity - if the condition of neutron composition is good enough and calculated enough, no matter stability, then **any** element is able to be the baseline hydrogen is. Thus, bring us back to Act II, and the dissemination problem - what is even the *prime matter*?

#### The anti-atomist movement, and positivist challenge (1840s-1890s)

The second crisis is rather philosophical, much less relevant to the game of theoretical-empirical pushback, but much more interesting per perspectives. And best of such, it is relevant to the failure modes often reside in the formation process itself. 

Figures of such crisis, Ernst Mach and Wilhelm Ostwald, were philosophically opposed to hypotheses about reality altogether, in which the picture of physics seems inadequate of their perception. Specifically, only energy as part of thermodynamics should be the basis of physical models, and of which often would be enough for all dynamical interactive theory on compositions itself. Such is often called *energeticists* as a sub-category in all and of all, and it would be to their intended effect. 

> … the biological-economical interpretation of the cognitive process can perfectly well co-exist on peaceable, and indeed on friendly, terms with that of present-day physics. The only real point of difference which has so far come to light concerns the belief in the reality of atoms. Here again, Planck can hardly find words degrading enough for such wrong headedness …. After exhorting the reader, with Christian charity, to respect his opponent, P. brands me, in the well-known biblical words, as a “false prophet.” It appears that the physicists are on the way to founding a church; they are already using a church’s traditional weapons. To this I answer simply: “If belief in the reality of atoms is so important to you, I cut myself off from the physicist’s mode of thinking, I do not wish to be a true physicist, I renounce all scientific respect—in short: I decline with thanks the communion of the faithful. I prefer freedom of thought.” [“The Guiding Principles of My Scientific Theory of Knowledge and Its Reception by My Contemporaries.” 37–38] - Ernst Mach.

The claim at such, similar to how the *equivalentists* like Marcellin Berthelot pronounced, is that the position of the Daltonian theory and framework was useful as the bookkeeping device, but positing the actual stance of *indivisibility*, is indeed a metaphysical overreach that would do the theory no good, and of which the Aristotle's ladder struck again in this instance. The atomic program is in dispute of the tension between the two criterion. The atomists are claiming what to be said as *Aristotle invariance* - where elemental identity grounds material identity through real compositional units, if such are to exist in full. The other side of anti-atomists are claiming functional invariance, the equivalent weight works, so the question of what underlies it is not scientifically meaning, nor it is justified because of the overreach to claim that it is the baseline where atoms will not be able to be divided, preceded any form of empirical details that would then refute it in practice, which did happen. In all, it is not that much difficult to see where this overreach occurs. As stated, the theory of **Daltonian principle** for irreducible atom proclaimed a specific *minimal floor* for all matters of being in the supposed *philosophical reality* observed and experienced of the physicists. There, as such, means there will have to exist the principle *prime atom*, of which Prout analyzed and hypothesized as such. But, even then, the evidences are not clear, there exists various empirical results in which denied such results and so on. So the claim it already overloaded with assertion instead, of which is trying to sell the story that there exists nothing beneath the atomic unit structure. It also conveniently disregard the epistemology of *what the atom is*, which we discussed above, that hinges on less of operational account, but for more instead relying on the ontological knowledge and of which to fully realize the given ontology. Per usual, it would be the reverse, where inference of the world is returned to the question on ontology of what are observed, yet in such case, anti-atomist movement retained the right kind of skepticism, which is never provided of a justified proof rather than just a small refutation. As there is, the stoichiometry of the time requires only two rules, the *law of definite proportion*, and the *law of multiple proportion*, such is to state as, respectively,

> I shall conclude by deducing from these experiments the principle I have established at the commencement of this memoir, viz. that iron, like many other metals, is subject to the law of nature which presides at every true combination, that is to say, that it unites with two constant proportions of oxygen. In this respect, it does not differ from tin, mercury, and lead, and, in a word, almost every known combustible.

and

> ..where two bodies combine in different proportions, if the quantity of one of them be assumed as a fixed number, the proportions of the other body that unite to it are in the simplest possible ratio to each other, being produced by multiplying the lowest proportion by a simple integral number as 2, 3, 4, &c. [...] in all cases the simple elements of bodies are disposed to unite atom to atom singly; or if either is in excess, it exceeds by a ratio to be expressed by some simple multiple of the number of its atoms.

All of which would be rather functionally enough, as said in the anti-atomist dispute. But, implicitly, Daltonian analysis above nullified quite much the border where the theory would fail, and such to say that it connects to an interesting phenomenon: where it is observed in even contemporary chemical theory, a given law is often not so much effective without the myriad of worse-case situations, and failure points that require another *proliferated special law*, branched as such, but perform again pattern matching dressed in formalized axiomatization works. Ironically, it is the chemist that suffered from this the most, as their textbooks are getting bigger every year to accommodate more and more special law of certain regions of interest. We do not need to say much about the rest of them, aside from the closure. The anti-atomist position was only decisively defeated by Perrin's measurements of Brownian motion (1908), which gave a direct determination of Avogadro's number consistent with kinetic theory - and by Thomson's electron, which demonstrated that if atoms were not real, something was coming out of them. However, we are still in the 19th. There are a few more crises. 

#### The cathode ray debate and particle-waves duality (1870s-1897)

While people would love to think about particle of waves, in the sense of optical physics and the old Newton-Huygens debate, the tortuous part of the path to Thomson, Rutherford and the pudding model is actually the *cathode ray tube experiment*. The typical story is rather not exposed enough, while simple, marks a rather long historical debate of sort. Cathode effect is not an obscure anomaly, due history: in fact, its earliest discovery was often attributed to Faraday. In 1838, Faraday observed what was called the **Faraday's dark space**, a dark region in a glow discharge near the negative electrode. The experiment is rather simple - passed a current through a rarefied air-filled glass tube and noticed a strange light arc with its beginning at the cathode (negative electrode) and its end almost at the anode (positive electrode), of which gives the dark space in apparent observations. Further then, per [@Busch2023XrayPriority] historical accounts, such cathode ray has been observed, though invisible, in experiments of early vacuum tubes when they struck the glass wall of the tube, exciting atoms of the glass and causing them to emit light. They noted that objects placed in the tube in front of the cathode could cast a shadow on the glowing wall, and realized that something must be travelling in straight lines from the cathode. Later on, during the 1870s, the same observation occurs - but this time, William Crookes did it with a more sophisticated device.

> In the 1870s, British physicist William Crookes and others were able to evacuate rarefied tubes to a pressure below 10−6 atm. These were called Crookes tubes. Faraday had been the first to notice a dark space just in front of the cathode, where there was no luminescence. This came to be called the cathode dark space, Faraday dark space, or Crookes dark space.
> 
> Crookes found that as he pumped more air out of the tubes, the Faraday dark space spread down the tube from the cathode toward the anode, until the tube was totally dark. But at the anode (positive) end of the tube, the glass of the tube itself began to glow. What was happening was that as more air was pumped from the tubes, the electrons could travel farther, on average, before they struck a gas atom. By the time the tube was dark, most of the electrons could travel in straight lines from the cathode to the anode end of the tube without a collision. With no obstructions, these low mass particles were accelerated to high velocities by the voltage between the electrodes. These were the cathode rays. When they reached the anode end of the tube, they were travelling so fast that, although they were attracted to it, they often **flew past the anode and struck the back wall** of the tube. When they struck atoms in the glass wall, they excited their orbital electrons to higher energy levels, causing them to fluoresce.

Of course, what I just gave you is the account by [@IntroChemNuclearAtom], of introductory chemistry where it already presupposed the existence of electron. However, one must then understand how bizarre it is under Dalton's atomic theory that to say, pretty much enfranchising on such atom. Another figure of such time is Eilhard Wiedemann, with support or co-author of Heinrich Hertz, and Goldstein, of which believed it to be *aether waves*, new form of electromagnetic radiation, separated from what carried the electric current through the tube. While it might seem absurd now, such line of thought is particularly not surprising. There exists no concept for an electron at present - what have to do with another proliferation of the underlying system must be a form, or some kind of matter of same order that does not break the floor of which atom already determines it as. Whether it is particle, a corpuscular value that went out from the atom as its small diffusion or waves does not really matter. 

Coming to the year of 1897, J.J. Thomson produced three seminal papers, all of which can still be grouped into what we can know of the moment as the cathode ray advancement of 1890s, from the room of the Cavendish Laboratory Cambridge. His inquiry is rather light. He set out to discover and analyze of what the cathode ray is made of, by refining the old systems by Hertz and such, first by removing *air resistance*, which deliberately gave him a stronger beam, inside such vacuum, shooting it through a positive anode with a hole in it. The dynamics of the "corpuscles", of which he later called, does not matter much - what was then prioritized is the apparent existence of the matter itself. By using Johnstone Stoney proposal in 1978 of the existence of an electric charge carrier of uniformly large charge associated with atoms, coined electron, Thomson succeeded in providing the first experimental proof by 1897, 

> "As the cathode rays carry a charge of negative electricity, are deflected by an electrostatic force as if they were negatively electrified, and are acted on by a magnetic force in just the way in which this force would act on a negatively electrified body moving along the path of these rays, I can see no escape from the conclusion that they are charges of negative electricity carried by particles of matter"

The elaboration into what we know of the present as the $e/m$-identification experiment, he found that each of the particles had the same small mass, about approximately $1/2000$ of the mass of a hydrogen, which, if we remember from what Prout was after, was once the proponent for the basis of the entire universal atomic model. Those experiments led him to at that time, far further than when such model t exist, believe that these particles were a basic constituent of matter; which influenced the decision, or rather the idea proposal of which can be said as atom, plus electron. The reason why such model *still retain* electron is also not a crude story either. When you have electron, smaller than the constituent part of which the entire periodic table was built on, you can only ask - where the electron is attached on such model? The way to imagine that, is to get them being absorbed, or stuck on the surface of what is said to be the atom, plumbing inside as part of the atom. That is where the **plum pudding model** was, and should be clear once we enter the Thomson atomic model. 



### The Thomson Atomic Model

Per [@thomson1904structure], [@thomson1907corpuscular], [@thomson1897cathode], [@thomson1903magnetic], [@thomson1904electricity], [@hon2013myth] and [@renstrom2022textbook], J.J. Thomson relied on his corpus of work into the electrical properties and so on of the **electron**, of which he himself discovered in which the Nobel Prize in Physics of 1906 was given. Generally speaking before going in any further details, the setup, despite its myriad of different results and motivation that led to such, is rather simple, and quite interesting. For the lack of a better description and of its weirdness,

> Scientists had now established that the atom was not indivisible as Dalton had believed, and due to the work of Thomson, Millikan, and others, the charge and mass of the negative, subatomic particles—the electrons—were known. However, the positively charged part of an atom was not yet well understood. In 1904, Thomson proposed the **“plum pudding”** model of atoms, which described a positively charged mass with an equal amount of negative charge in the form of electrons embedded in it, since all atoms are electrically neutral. A competing model had been proposed in 1903 by *Hantaro Nagaoka*, who postulated a Saturn-like atom, consisting of a positively charged sphere surrounded by a **halo** of electrons.
